To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vaccinating virus-carriers with a gH/L fusion protein improves their ability to neutralize virus infection.
vaccination with a gH-gL fusion protein improved the ability of MHV-68 carriers to neutralize virus.
vaccination with a gH-gL fusion protein improves virus neutralization in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a vaccine against herpes simplex virus (HSV) infection.
how the immune system controls infection.
understanding the immune response to gammaherpesviroses, and developing new strategies for controlling infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the post-exposure gH/gL vaccination of virus carriers can improve their antibody response to MHV-68 and thereby improve their capacity for virus control.
post-exposure vaccination with gH/gL protein can improve the neutralizing capacity of the immune system of MHV-68 carriers and thus may help reduce transmission of the virus.
vaccination with a gH-gL fusion protein can improve the capacity for virus neutralisation in MHV-68 carriers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vaccination of virus carriers with the gH/gL protein improves virus neutralization, and that gH/gl is a major target for neutralization.
vaccinating carriers with a fusion protein improves the capacity for virus neutralisation in vitro and in the mouse.
post-exposure vaccination can improve gammaherpesviral neutralization by enhancing the neutralization potential of the host's antibody response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vaccination can improve the antibody response of virus carriers.
post-exposure vaccination can improve the neutralizing capacity of the immune system.
vaccinating herpesvirus carriers with a gB or gH/gL vaccine could improve their ability to block infection.
